context:
Goal: the q_max browser run takes as long as the checks need, no longer (your words on 258).
Problem (goal): lane qmax-browser-slow-checks (q_max #1032) found three causes. It fixed the fixed sleeps (-15 to -18%). Two causes stay. Each page load on the dev server fetches 423 files (29-47% of the time). Each failing check waits 30 s (4,184 s of a 10,587 s run).
Based on (ruling): your 258 note, 21:32 CST Nov 5, "the run can't be doing things right if it needs that long": find the cause, not a cap or a split. Asked again because the fix for the two causes left changes how the checks run.
Based on (measured): the lane's profile of each Playwright call, Nov 5.
Departs from: q_max main runs browser checks on the Vite dev server, with Playwright's 30 s wait — a moves them to a production build; b cuts the wait to 5 s.

Meanwhile: #1032 finishes its review; nothing else waits.
home: q_max .github/workflows/browser.yml; D-542, the browser tier runs on your dispatch

lastAnswer.note: Question withdrawn 23:20 CST Nov 5. The coordinator took a itself under your 21:32 ask (find the cause), since it can be undone: lane qmax-browser-prod-build runs the browser checks on a production build. b, the 5 s wait, is dropped as a bandaid. The item closes when both q_max lanes merge.

options.gain: Each page load drops most of its cost. This fixes a cause.
options.label: Run the browser checks on a production build
options.lose: A check no longer runs against the dev server you use day to day.

options.gain: A failing check costs 5 s, not 30 s (the slowest passing action took 0.5 s).
options.label: Cut each action's wait to about 5 s
options.lose: It hides the cost: the failing checks are the real cause, and a slow but correct step could fail.

options.label: Both, a first
options.lose: Two lanes, and each needs a full-tier run.

title: q_max browser run: two slow causes left. Fix which?
why: Recommended: a. The run finishes with no more work; b saves wait time but costs a build lane and the same runner minutes.
